Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Business outlets are dominated by a sharp global stock selloff tied to anxiety over AI capital spending, after disappointing reactions to Meta and Tesla earnings sent tech shares and bonds swinging, compounded by escalating Middle East tensions pushing oil prices higher. Secondary threads include a global PHP cybersecurity scramble, fallout from France's bond-market crisis, and AI-driven corporate cost-cutting (Barclays' layoffs).

stories.headline: Tech-led selloff deepens as AI spending fears and Mideast tensions rattle markets
stories.summary: A selloff in technology giants and escalating Middle East hostilities drove stocks toward their worst session since July, with Meta sinking over 7% and chipmakers hit hard as investors questioned whether massive AI spending is paying off, while Treasuries rallied on haven demand.

stories.headline: Oil surges, Saudi airport attacked as Iran-U.S. standoff escalates
stories.summary: Oil prices jumped more than 2%, with Brent above $111 a barrel, as traders weighed renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and the risk of further U.S.-Iran hostilities, while the U.S. ordered some staff to leave Riyadh after an airport attack killed one person.

stories.headline: Barclays to cut 5,000 jobs in AI-driven efficiency push
stories.summary: Barclays plans to cut 5,000 jobs, with the bank saying it believes it can operate more efficiently with fewer workers because of artificial intelligence, the latest major employer to tie headcount reductions directly to AI adoption.

stories.headline: Critical PHP flaw sparks global rush to patch websites
stories.summary: Governments and businesses worldwide scrambled to patch a newly discovered, AI-uncovered security flaw in PHP, the programming language underpinning a large share of the internet, after it knocked sites offline.

stories.headline: France's debt crisis deepens as foreign investors retreat
stories.summary: Foreign capital that finances France appears to be reversing course, investors say, worsening a fall selloff in French bonds that intensified after riots last weekend, with 10-year yields hitting a 24-year high.

stories.headline: Blackstone cuts property valuations, core businesses squeezed by rates
stories.summary: Blackstone's private-equity asset-sale proceeds fell 49% as rising rates squeeze its core businesses, while the firm's president said rising market volatility has stalled a quick return of cash to investors through IPOs.

stories.headline: Zuckerberg's deal to keep Meta in California, new share class for AI fundraising
stories.summary: Mark Zuckerberg struck an agreement to keep Meta in California, underscoring business fears about a major state tax proposal, as Meta separately created a new non-voting share class that could let it raise AI-related funds while preserving his control.

stories.headline: Elon Musk invests roughly $1 billion in Skydance
stories.summary: Elon Musk is investing about $1 billion in Skydance, a deal with ties to Larry Ellison, whose son David Ellison runs the studio.

Business.gaps: Puck had no relevant business coverage found in the last 48 hours; Forbes, The Information, Fortune, Washington Post and Axios content was available via search, while WSJ, NYT, FT, The Economist, Politico, Business Insider and BBC were drawn only from the provided feed items since they block search.

US politics.overview: With just under two weeks until the midterms, US political outlets are converging on a rapidly deteriorating environment for Republicans, as nonpartisan handicappers shift dozens of House and Senate races toward Democrats and Trump's approval sinks to record lows. Coverage also centers on a fake-pollster scandal roiling campaigns, DOJ voter-fraud crackdowns colliding with courts, and security concerns from threatening letters sent to lawmakers and election offices nationwide.

stories.headline: Cook Political Report keeps shifting races toward Democrats as GOP position erodes
stories.summary: Cook Political Report moved South Carolina and Mississippi Senate races toward Democrats while shifting Minnesota toward the GOP, part of a broader wave that has now moved 11 more House districts and several Senate races away from Republicans this month, with Decision Desk HQ putting the GOP's chance of holding the House at just 22%.

stories.headline: How a fake pollster may have moved some 2026 elections
stories.summary: Politico reports that Wedgewood Polls admitted fabricating survey results, with some candidates saying the fake numbers damaged their campaigns just weeks before Election Day.

stories.headline: DOJ's noncitizen voter crackdown collides with courts days before midterms
stories.summary: A federal judge ordered DHS to halt noncitizen-voting probes in battleground states citing intimidation concerns, even as a federal prosecutor said DOJ had verified 20,000 flagged California voter-roll entries as noncitizens — a claim Los Angeles County election officials call unreliable.

stories.headline: AIPAC halts endorsements and direct campaign contributions
stories.summary: The pro-Israel lobbying group AIPAC announced it would stop endorsing candidates or giving directly to campaigns, though its affiliated super PAC will keep spending, a shift that follows the group's brand becoming a liability in several Democratic primaries this cycle.

stories.headline: Suspicious letters with white powder hit Congress and election offices nationwide
stories.summary: Axios reports that over three dozen lawmakers and election offices in at least 32 states have received suspicious letters, many containing a white powder, forcing evacuations and prompting an FBI investigation just weeks before the midterms.

stories.headline: Supreme Court weighs border wall construction and other Trump-era emergency appeals
stories.summary: The Trump administration has asked the justices to let border wall construction continue, one of several high-stakes interim-docket disputes SCOTUSblog is tracking alongside cases on transgender inmate policy and third-country removals.

stories.headline: Top Virginia Democrat indicted on cannabis enterprise conspiracy charges
stories.summary: The Justice Department indicted Virginia state Senate President Pro Tempore Louise Lucas and seven others, accusing the longtime Democratic leader of using her political clout to conceal an illegal cannabis sales operation.

stories.headline: House Republicans quietly scale back redistricting hopes as climate sours
stories.summary: Axios reports House Republicans privately worry their nationwide mid-decade redistricting push could net just one seat overall, down from hopes of a 10-seat boost, as GOP support erodes among Latino voters in Texas and Florida and Democrats' California countermap puts five seats in play.

US politics.gaps: Politico, NYT, WSJ and The Guardian block web search, so coverage from those outlets is limited to the feed items provided; no recent NOTUS items beyond older cached pages were found via search, and no distinct Punchbowl News scoop from the last 24-48 hours was located beyond its Arizona healthcare-messaging piece.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across tech and AI outlets is dominated by big tech earnings and the money behind the AI buildout (Meta's new AI-funding stock class, Tesla's falling profits), a global scramble to patch the severe PHP2Shell vulnerability, and fresh signs of AI-fueled market jitters and cyber threats including a China-linked breach. Several outlets are also tracking the agentic AI product race (Anthropic's Claude Duet, Meta's Muse) and questions about AI's geopolitical and physical footprint, from chips reaching China despite export controls to data-center water and pollution fights.

stories.headline: Meta creates new non-voting share class to fund its AI buildout
stories.summary: Meta is issuing a new class of non-voting stock to raise capital for its AI investments while preserving Mark Zuckerberg's voting control, and The Information reports the move was also shaped by worries about California's wealth-tax Proposition 40. A related filing shows Meta's total future lease and contract commitments have swelled to roughly $825 billion.

stories.headline: AI-fueled stock jitters and Mideast tensions spark a broad market retreat
stories.summary: Big tech earnings reports have spooked investors even as oil prices jump to multi-month highs, with Bloomberg and WSJ both noting a flight to Treasuries as traders reassess the AI trade; The Economist separately argues AI compute itself is becoming a tradeable commodity needing new financial markets.

stories.headline: Hackers race to exploit critical PHP2Shell flaw before patches land
stories.summary: Cloudflare and AWS say exploitation of the PHP2Shell flaws began days before a patch was released, with millions of attempts now logged and government agencies warning companies to act immediately; The Information notes the bugs affect roughly 70% of the world's websites and AI tools helped both find and exploit them.

stories.headline: Tesla's profit drops 43% as it ramps Optimus robot production and pushes Cybercab sales
stories.summary: Tesla's revenue was flat while expenses jumped as it accelerated spending on Optimus robots, AI and autonomous driving; separately the company said it will begin selling its Cybercab to customers by year's end even as regulators probe whether the vehicle meets safety standards, and The Information reports Musk declined to discuss a possible SpaceX-Tesla merger.

stories.headline: Microsoft says Chinese state-linked hackers used AI agents to breach thousands of cloud tenants via ConnectWise
stories.summary: Microsoft reported that a breach of ConnectWise gave Chinese state-linked attackers access to roughly 2,250 cloud tenants, with AI agents automating parts of the intrusion and privileged access gained in some environments in under three hours; The Information identifies the AI agent used as Artex.

stories.headline: Nvidia Blackwell Ultra chips found linked to China Telecom despite US export controls
stories.summary: Israeli security firm Lava found 32 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 chips connected to systems linked to state-owned China Telecom, raising fresh questions about enforcement of US chip export restrictions, per The Information's reporting as aggregated by Techmeme.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches 'Claude Duet,' a proactive always-on agent to rival Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots
stories.summary: Anthropic has launched Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent built on Claude Opus 5.5 that can handle tasks even while the user is offline, directly challenging Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots in the race for always-on consumer agents. VentureBeat notes Duet's $20 monthly entry price undercuts rival subscription tiers, though Muse offers a free option.

stories.headline: DeepMind's Hassabis shortens his AGI timeline to two to three years
stories.summary: Demis Hassabis has moved up his forecast for artificial general intelligence, now expecting it within two to three years, down from his previous three-to-five-year estimate, underscoring the accelerating confidence among top AI lab leaders.

Tech & AI.gaps: No recent coverage could be verified directly from The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist, Google DeepMind, OpenAI or The Guardian beyond the specific feed items and search snippets already cited; Platformer's search results returned only older archived material, so current Platformer coverage could not be confirmed.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are dominated by the oil price spike tied to escalating Middle East conflict (Saudi attacks, U.S.-Iran tensions), alongside major nuclear power announcements in the U.S. and sobering new climate science on the 1.5C warming limit. Trade-focused outlets (Utility Dive, Heatmap) are also tracking data center-driven demand growth, rising electricity bills, and policy fights over utility mergers and tariffs.

stories.headline: Oil prices surge as Mideast conflict escalates
stories.summary: Brent crude climbed above $111 a barrel as traders reacted to renewed attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and fears of further U.S.-Iran hostilities, sending ripples through global markets.

stories.headline: The Nuclear Company unveils massive Kentucky reactor project
stories.summary: The Nuclear Company announced plans for 6.6 gigawatts of new large-scale reactors at a greenfield Kentucky site dubbed Prosperity One, aiming for a Chinese-style buildout with up to six AP1000 units on one site to drive down costs.

stories.headline: UN report: chance to avoid breaching 1.5C has been lost
stories.summary: A new UN Environment Programme assessment concludes a temporary breach of the 1.5C warming limit is now inevitable after decades of insufficient climate action.

stories.headline: Expensive gas blamed for nearly 90% of UK electricity bill rises
stories.summary: A Carbon Brief analysis finds that a surge in wholesale gas costs is responsible for nearly 90% of the increase in UK household electricity bills.

stories.headline: Google strikes 1-gigawatt virtual power plant deal with Voltus
stories.summary: Google and VPP operator Voltus announced plans to add 1 gigawatt of clean capacity over three to four years, funding demand-response resources across the strained PJM grid to help meet surging data center power needs.

stories.headline: Virginia governor pushes for 6-year rate freeze in Dominion-NextEra merger review
stories.summary: Gov. Abigail Spanberger is asking regulators to impose a six-year rate freeze and raise Dominion's debt share if they approve its merger with NextEra, aiming to lower the utility's rate of return.

stories.headline: IPCC meeting in Ethiopia ends without agreement on timeline, again
stories.summary: Countries failed for the sixth consecutive time to agree on a publishing timeline for the IPCC's next major climate assessment, leaving scientists and observers frustrated.

stories.headline: Solar PPA prices jump 5% in Q3 as new trade tariffs bite
stories.summary: LevelTen data shows solar power purchase agreement prices rose 5% in the third quarter largely due to new tariffs, while wind PPA prices held steadier but may also rise as tariffs take effect.

Energy.gaps: E&E News' public site stopped publishing new content after August 31 (it has moved behind POLITICO Pro), so no verified last-48-hours coverage could be confirmed; Canary Media's homepage showed mostly evergreen/about content without clear new leads in the window; Latitude Media's most prominent items (e.g., Google-Constellation nuclear deal, Voltus funding round) were dated slightly outside the strict 48-hour window but are noted where relevant.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across these outlets clusters around escalating EU-China trade friction, fresh elite-level corruption and political intrigue inside China, corporate earnings divergences at major Chinese firms (CATL, Huawei's Seres partnership), labor unrest tied to the AI boom at Micron's Taiwan plant, and renewed diplomatic maneuvering toward a possible Trump-Xi-Putin summit. Taiwan-focused outlets are also fixated on a China-linked attack on a comedian and the fallout for cross-strait tensions.

stories.headline: Who blinked first? EU-China trade peace descends into war of words
stories.summary: Less than two weeks after Brussels and Beijing struck a deal to avert an escalating trade dispute, the two sides are now publicly sparring over who made the first concession, underscoring how fragile the truce remains.

stories.headline: Trump envoy asks Putin to resume three-way talks with China
stories.summary: A Trump envoy pressed Putin to restart three-way summit talks as Washington pushes to end the Ukraine war; Caixin reported separately that Trump said he is open to meeting Xi and Putin in China, on the sidelines of a gathering planned for Shenzhen next month.

stories.headline: Son of former Chongqing mayor Huang Qifan taken away by authorities
stories.summary: Chinese authorities reportedly detained the son of former Chongqing mayor Huang Qifan, a once-prominent economic official and ally of disgraced politician Bo Xilai; Nikkei Asia separately reported that Huang himself, long seen as a political survivor, is now under investigation.

stories.headline: CATL's profit growth lags far behind surging revenue
stories.summary: CATL's third-quarter revenue jumped 58.6% year-on-year to 165.22 billion yuan while net profit grew just 14.5%, a gap Caixin reported sent CATL shares tumbling as lower-margin energy-storage deliveries and new tax policies weighed on earnings.

stories.headline: Huawei's auto ambitions face a reckoning after Seres rift
stories.summary: Caixin's lead investigative piece examines strains over control and mounting costs between automaker Seres and Huawei in their flagship Aito EV brand, even after the two firms signed a new five-year partnership agreement on October 1.

stories.headline: Micron Taiwan workers strike over AI-profit sharing
stories.summary: Workers representing about 70% of staff at Micron's Taoyuan, Taiwan plant staged a 24-hour strike demanding a guaranteed quarterly bonus pool equal to 15% of operating profit, after an AI-driven earnings boom, even as the company's larger Taichung plant union separately reached a profit-linked bonus deal.

stories.headline: Taiwan charges five over plot to run over comedian who joked about Xi Jinping
stories.summary: Taiwan prosecutors indicted five people for allegedly staging a traffic collision that injured a comedian who had satirized Xi Jinping, after being paid by a Chinese national; Taiwan's security bureau says such incidents reflect intensifying and more targeted Chinese transnational repression ahead of November elections.

stories.headline: New research tries to defuse the "China shock"
stories.summary: The Economist covers a heated academic dispute over an influential and long-cited study on how Chinese import competition reshaped global manufacturing employment, as researchers revisit its findings and methodology.

China.gaps: China Daily, Xinhua and Yicai Global had no distinct, recent China-specific stories surfaced in search beyond general/archived content; CGTN's only current item was a ceremonial Xi Jinping speech marking the Long March anniversary. Reuters, AP, FT, NYT and WSJ block web search and had no relevant items in the provided feed, so they could not be assessed.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf and Middle East outlets is dominated by fears of renewed US-Israel military action against Iran after the US midterms, continuing Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabian airports and oil infrastructure, and Israel's tense October 27 election pitting Netanyahu against Gadi Eisenkot. Oil markets, Gaza's worsening humanitarian conditions, and Gulf diplomatic maneuvering (UAE's UN bid, Turkey-hosted regional talks) are also drawing heavy attention.

stories.headline: US and Israel draw up plans for post-midterm strikes on Iran
stories.summary: Reports say Washington and Israel have prepared a short, intensive three-day campaign targeting Iran's nuclear sites, energy infrastructure and missile arsenal for after the November 3 US midterms, with Trump declaring 'something is going to happen very soon, one way or another' even as he has not yet authorized action.

stories.headline: Deadly Houthi attacks on Saudi airports continue, US orders embassy staff to leave
stories.summary: Jordan and Egypt condemned a new Houthi-claimed attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam that killed one person and injured eight, part of a weeks-long campaign of strikes on Saudi aviation infrastructure that has also prompted Washington to order non-essential diplomatic staff out of the kingdom.

stories.headline: Israel's election becomes referendum on Netanyahu as Eisenkot surges
stories.summary: With Israel's election days away, FT frames the vote as a battle for the country's future, while Al-Monitor notes both Netanyahu and challenger Gadi Eisenkot oppose Palestinian statehood even as polls show Eisenkot ahead and pollsters debating whether Netanyahu's late push can still secure a majority.

stories.headline: Oil prices rally and Iran's shadow tanker fleet runs dry amid escalation
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports a flight to Treasuries as tech-earnings disappointment and escalating Middle East hostilities pushed oil prices higher, while WSJ and the Jerusalem Post separately report Iran's floating oil reserves used for China sales have been completely depleted after a months-long US blockade.

stories.headline: Gaza families brace for 'another famine' as UN cuts food aid
stories.summary: Middle East Eye reports funding shortages will leave roughly half a million Gazans without critical food assistance, compounding a live-blogged toll of Palestinians killed daily by Israeli fire, including a teenage girl.

stories.headline: UAE nominates Lana Nusseibeh to lead the UN amid criticism over Sudan, Israel policy
stories.summary: The UAE has put forward diplomat Lana Nusseibeh, who is of Palestinian descent, as its candidate for UN Secretary-General, a bid drawing scrutiny over Abu Dhabi's record on Sudan and its ties to Israel.

stories.headline: Houthi attacks trigger foreign investor sell-off in Saudi markets, FII forum cancelled
stories.summary: AGBI reports oil climbed near $110 a barrel after renewed Houthi attack claims and Iranian threats, while separate coverage notes foreign investors have been pulling out of Saudi equities and the Future Investment Initiative forum was cancelled following the strikes.

stories.headline: Israeli settlers escalate attacks on Palestinian olive harvest in West Bank
stories.summary: Al-Monitor reports Israeli settlers have intensified violent attacks on Palestinian farmers during the olive harvest in the West Bank, a story that coincides with WSJ reporting that US congressional candidate Brad Lander says he was detained by the Israeli military while accompanying Palestinians during the harvest.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not retrieve recent distinct coverage from Arabian Business, Zawya, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, The New Arab, Ynetnews, or Iran International within the search allowance; AP, NYT and The Economist blocked web search and had no relevant feed items provided.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage across these outlets centers on escalating political and security crises — DRC's Kabila-led insurgency and Tanzania's opposition crackdown — alongside Ebola containment efforts in East Africa and a cluster of economic stories spanning South Africa's budget, media M&A, and a major Madagascar financing deal.

stories.headline: Belgium condemns Kabila's launch of political-military group in DRC
stories.summary: Belgium has condemned former Congolese president Joseph Kabila's launch of a new political-military movement ten days earlier as deplorable and unacceptable, as the move turns an eastern insurgency into an explicit bid for national power.

stories.headline: Second Tanzanian opposition figure faces death penalty after treason charges
stories.summary: A senior Chadema opposition official, John Pambalu, is facing the death penalty after being charged with treason, signaling an intensifying crackdown on Tanzania's opposition.

stories.headline: Nine Ebola Cases Have Kenya Holding Its Breath
stories.summary: Kenyan health authorities are waiting to see whether swift quarantine measures were enough to prevent a full-blown Ebola outbreak after nine cases emerged.

stories.headline: South Africa's mid-term budget: Fiscal armour hardens, but can Pretoria drive regional growth?
stories.summary: South Africa stabilized debt and widened its primary surplus in the mid-term budget, though a growth downgrade to 1.2% highlights the struggle to translate fiscal discipline into regional growth.

stories.headline: Niger: Two Western hostages released in Libya after 18 months in Islamic State captivity
stories.summary: Two European women held by Islamic State militants in Niger have been freed and flown to Benghazi following mediation led by Saddam Haftar.

stories.headline: CANAL+ faces a South African turnaround test as MultiChoice revenue falls 3%
stories.summary: CANAL+ is banking on new DStv packages and stronger content to revive MultiChoice in South Africa after its revenue fell 3% in the nine months to September 2026.

stories.headline: Gemcorp joins Madagascar to raise $5bn for energy, mining
stories.summary: Madagascar is partnering with asset manager Gemcorp Capital Management in an effort to raise as much as $5 billion to fund energy, infrastructure and mining projects on the island.

stories.headline: Côte d'Ivoire: Could a new court battle cost opposition leader Tidjane Thiam his party?
stories.summary: Ivorian courts are preparing to hear challenges from PDCI members seeking to annul exiled opposition leader Tidjane Thiam's election as party chief.

Africa.gaps: Africa Confidential, The Continent and African Business had no clearly dated items within the last 24-48 hours in search results (their most recent identifiable pieces were from several days to weeks earlier); Reuters, AP, BBC and FT block search and had no relevant items in the provided feed, so they could not be assessed.

Media.overview: Media-industry coverage over the past 48 hours centers on publishers' escalating fight with Big Tech over AI scraping and licensing terms, a wave of Q3 earnings from Comcast and Spotify, and ongoing turmoil inside CBS News and CNN as both navigate new ownership and White House press-access fights. Trade outlets are also tracking a fresh round of journalism layoffs and newsroom drama, from BBC job cuts to an ESPN booth feud.

stories.headline: UK politicians and German publishers push regulators to pause Meta's new terms before Oct 30 deadline
stories.summary: British lawmakers and German publishers are urging regulators to halt Meta's sweeping new commercial terms before they take effect, with the UK's competition authority having sent Meta a formal letter seeking talks on the change.

stories.headline: Canadian publishers sue Anthropic as Google's AI news pilot expands to CNN and Reach
stories.summary: Postmedia, Torstar, The Globe and Mail and The Canadian Press have filed a copyright suit against Anthropic over its Claude model, even as Google says more than 400 publications, now including CNN and Reach, have joined its paid news AI pilot.

stories.headline: CNN threatens new legal action over White House blocking Air Force One, Oval Office access
stories.summary: CNN told the Trump administration it will pursue further legal action if the White House keeps barring its journalists from Air Force One and the Oval Office, while the White House Correspondents' Association separately accused the administration of "retaliation" after a reporter was blocked from a press gathering.

stories.headline: Peacock posts second straight quarterly profit as Comcast's broadband slide continues
stories.summary: Comcast's Peacock streaming service logged a $261 million profit for a second consecutive quarter, even as the parent company continues to be dragged down by broadband and video subscriber losses.

stories.headline: Spotify tops 306 million premium subscribers as revenue jumps 16%
stories.summary: Spotify reported strong Q3 growth with monthly active users rising 11% to 788 million, and the company is positioning itself to benefit from the rise of AI shopping and voice agents.

stories.headline: CBS pairs DraftKings branding with Election Night coverage, stirring internal unease
stories.summary: Status reports that CBS's owned-and-operated stations will carry DraftKings sponsorship branding through Election Night, a tie-up that has reportedly unsettled some inside the network.

stories.headline: Bari Weiss's CBS News remains a lightning rod a year into her tenure
stories.summary: Puck's Dylan Byers argues the relentless media-reporter fixation on Bari Weiss reflects broader anxieties about the news business, even as her CBS News leadership shows signs of maturing.

stories.headline: Troy Aikman and Joe Buck's ESPN partnership nearly boiled over into a physical confrontation
stories.summary: A new report details weeks of rising tension between ESPN broadcast partners Troy Aikman and Joe Buck that reportedly culminated in a heated, near-physical clash.

Media.gaps: No recent coverage found from CJR beyond feature/opinion pieces, and NYT, WSJ, FT and The Guardian block web search so only their feed items (largely outside this topic) could be used; no qualifying Guardian media-industry item was found in the feed.
